definitions.definition: ∂ denotes ordinary coordinate partial differentiation, component by component for vector-valued functions. Subscripts t and tt denote one and two time derivatives, x_j and x_jx_j denote one and two derivatives in spatial coordinate j, and x_jt denotes first time then spatial differentiation. Thus u_t=∂_t u, u_tt=∂_t∂_t u and ∂_{x_j}u_t=∂_{x_j}∂_t u. The same notation applies to any differentiable real scalar function. Derivatives are used only where their existence has been established. For native total-function source applications, a function on Ω may be extended by zero outside Ω; at points of Ω all derivatives refer to its germ on Ω, independent of the extension.

definitions.definition: e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|²+Σ_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u(x,t)|². All norms are Euclidean; the spatial sum is the Frobenius square of the spatial gradient.
v·w=dot(v,w)=Σ_{k=1}^d v_k w_k for v,w∈ℝ^d and any finite dimension d; |v|²=v·v.

output.statement: All positive-order partial derivatives of u are smooth on Ω; e and e_t are continuous there. For every (x,t)∈Ω, u·u_t=0 and u_t·(u_tt−Δ_xu)=0, and e_t=2u_t·u_tt+2Σ_{j=1}^n ∂_{x_j}u·∂_{x_j}u_t. Mixed time and spatial second derivatives agree. At each such point, every scalar a satisfying u_tt−Δ_xu=a u equals Σ_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u|²−|u_t|².

locals.declaration: Choose a real a with u_tt(x,t)−Δ_xu(x,t)=a u(x,t), using H005 at (x,t).

argument.text: Fix arbitrary x∈ℝ^n and t>0. H002 is smoothness on the open set Ω. Repeatedly apply M009 over ℝ to the zero extension of u on Ω with both smoothness orders ∞; since ∞+1=∞ this gives smoothness of its iterated derivatives on Ω. Evaluation of these continuous multilinear derivatives on fixed coordinate vectors gives the ordinary smooth partial derivatives. M002, over ℝ at (x,t), with order 2, then gives equality of time-space mixed second derivatives, by evaluating the symmetric second derivative on the time and j-th spatial coordinate vectors. Finite sums, scalar products and products of smooth real components are smooth, so e and e_t are continuous. M001 applied along the time line to u with itself gives ∂_t(u·u)=2u·u_t. H004 says u·u=1 throughout Ω; its derivative is zero. Thus u·u_t=0. This calculation is valid at every point of Ω, so the identity holds throughout Ω, not only at the chosen point; it may therefore be differentiated along any time line in Ω.

produces.statement: All partial derivatives of u are smooth on Ω, e and e_t are continuous on Ω, mixed second time-space derivatives agree, and for every (y,r)∈Ω one has u(y,r)·u_t(y,r)=0.

argument.text: Choose a from H005 at (x,t). By F001 and the finite-sum definition of the scalar product, u_t·(u_tt−Δ_xu)=u_t·(a u)=a(u_t·u)=0. This uses no derivative or regularity of the selected scalar. For completeness, M001 along time, applied to u and u_t, differentiates the identity u·u_t=0 and yields |u_t|²+u·u_tt=0. Applying the same product rule first to u·u=1 and then to u·∂_{x_j}u=0 along any spatial coordinate line gives u·∂_{x_jx_j}u=−|∂_{x_j}u|². Dotting the normality equation with u and using u·u=1 therefore gives a=Σ_j|∂_{x_j}u|²−|u_t|². Since this calculation uses only the defining equation for a, it holds for every scalar satisfying it.

produces.statement: At (x,t), u_t·(u_tt−Δ_xu)=0; every scalar satisfying u_tt−Δ_xu=a u equals Σ_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u|²−|u_t|².

argument.text: M001 applied along time to u_t with itself gives ∂_t|u_t|²=2u_t·u_tt. Applied to ∂_{x_j}u with itself, it gives ∂_t|∂_{x_j}u|²=2∂_{x_j}u·∂_t∂_{x_j}u; the mixed-derivative equality of F001 replaces the last factor by ∂_{x_j}u_t. Differentiating the finite spatial sum gives e_t=2u_t·u_tt+2Σ_j∂_{x_j}u·∂_{x_j}u_t. Together with F001 and F002 this proves every clause of the output for the arbitrary point. The witness a does not escape: the assertion about it is universal conditional on its displayed equation.
